Exercises

Problems to check your understanding of this chapter. The solutions are folded away — try them yourself first.

Medium

1Medium

The whole economy cuts wages by 333.

With MPC c=0.6c = 0.6c=0.6, find (1) the change in output and jobs, and (2) the final wage bill. (100100100 workers, output 151515 each, starting wage 101010.)

  • The Two Faces of a Wage: One Firm vs the Whole Economy
Show solution

  1. (1) The first-round wage-bill loss is 3⋅100=3003 \cdot 100 = 3003⋅100=300; consumption falls by 0.6⋅300=1800.6 \cdot 300 = 1800.6⋅300=180. Through the multiplier 11−0.6=2.5\frac{1}{1 - 0.6} = 2.51−0.61​=2.5, output falls by 180⋅2.5=450180 \cdot 2.5 = 450180⋅2.5=450, from 150015001500 to 105010501050, and jobs land at 1050/15=701050 / 15 = 701050/15=70 — 303030 jobs gone.

  2. (2) The final wage bill is the new wage 777 times the surviving jobs 707070: 490490490.

    The fall is 510510510, nearly twice the intended 300300300 — when wages and jobs fall together, the wage bill feeds on itself.

    Through the one-firm lens the answer flips: the same cut lets one firm hire L=60−4⋅7=32L = 60 - 4 \cdot 7 = 32L=60−4⋅7=32, twelve MORE workers.

2Hard

The menu cost is F=8F = 8F=8 and the profit hill is π=100−2(p−p∗)2\pi = 100 - 2(p - p^*)^2π=100−2(p−p∗)2.

(1) Where is the edge δ∗\delta^*δ∗ of the inaction band?

(2) For shocks δ=1.5\delta = 1.5δ=1.5 and δ=2.5\delta = 2.5δ=2.5, what happens to the price and to volume?

(3) Among twelve firms drawing the scene's assorted shocks, how many keep their price?

  • Menu Costs: When Prices Won't Move
Show solution

  1. (1) The edge is where the standing-still loss 2δ22\delta^22δ2 equals the menu cost 888: δ∗=8/2=2\delta^* = \sqrt{8 / 2} = 2δ∗=8/2​=2. Shocks up to 222 are cheaper to swallow; past 222, cheaper to reprint.

  2. (2) At δ=1.5\delta = 1.5δ=1.5: the loss 2⋅1.52=4.5<82 \cdot 1.5^2 = 4.5 < 82⋅1.52=4.5<8, so the price stays at 101010 and volume falls to 50−5⋅1.5=42.550 - 5 \cdot 1.5 = 42.550−5⋅1.5=42.5. At δ=2.5\delta = 2.5δ=2.5: the loss 2⋅2.52=12.5>82 \cdot 2.5^2 = 12.5 > 82⋅2.52=12.5>8, so the price drops to 7.57.57.5 and volume recovers to 505050.

  3. (3) Firms whose shock lands inside the band edge 222 keep their price.

    Of the scene's shock list, from 0.250.250.25 to 444, eight values are at most 222, so 888 of 121212 firms (67%)(67\%)(67%) freeze their price and let quantities take the hit.

    The bigger the menu cost, the bigger that share — and the stickier the whole economy's prices.
